msg: STEP OVERSHOOT at /AIN_ADC - the node the converter samples, taken past R6 - on a 20 mV small-signal step with a 1 ns edge into the board load as fitted (R6 49.9 ohm, C7 1 nF, RON 50 ohm + C_SAMPLE 48 pF). Design promise: blocks.md s7 item 3, overshoot <= 5 %. Measured 0.141 %, i.e. 35x inside the bound. SEEDED DEFECT: R6 -> 0 (isolation resistor omitted, or shorted by a routing error) reads 73.4 % - the OPA320's 90 ohm open-loop RO working against C7 inside the loop. The bound is deliberately NOT written on the buffer output node; see the .cir header for the Cdif feedforward measurement that makes that node read 11.7 % on an edge the board cannot produce.

RINGBACK below the final value at /AIN_ADC, measured in a window that opens 0.5 us after the step - i.e. after the rise itself is complete (settle_ns = 197 ns). This is the measure that separates 'fast edge' from 'unstable': a healthy loop is flat here while a marginal one is still ringing microseconds later. Measured 0.00013 %. Under the R6 -> 0 defect it reads 16.4 %. Paired with os_adc_pct because a single-sided peak measure cannot tell a monotonic overshoot from an oscillation.

residual error on C_SAMPLE itself at the SAMPLE INSTANT t0 + 9.0 us, in uV - the charge the converter actually digitizes, not the node in front of it. Design promise: blocks.md s7 item 3, 'no ringing above 1/2 LSB at the sample instant'; 1/2 LSB at the ADC node = 15.6 uV (5.120 V full scale / 65536 = 78.1 uV per LSB). t_acq = 9.0 us is EXACT and host-immovable: tSMPL = 4.5 DCLOCK min at fDCLOCK 500 kHz is a CLOCK-CYCLE COUNT, not a CS dwell (state.json decision 54, C544731 abs_max 109/110). Measured 0.0 uV - below the solver floor.

MODEL CALIBRATION, not a board bound: slew rate of the same OPA320 boundary model at TI's OWN test condition - CL = 50 pF, G = +1, 2 V step, nothing else on the output - against SR = 10 V/us typ (SBOS513F p.8, C92494.json abs_max 44). Measured 9.996 V/us. This is what pins the min/max transconductance clamp; a soft tanh limiter read 6.53 here and was rejected for it. Measured over 30-70 % of the step so both ends stay inside the slew-limited region (the amp leaves slew only when the input error falls below 79.6 mV).

the slew rate actually achieved into the BOARD load, 7.79 V/us against 10.0 V/us at TI's test load. Not a defect and not a design promise - it is a real consequence of this board's operating point: slewing C7 = 1 nF at 10 V/us asks 10 mA through the 90 ohm open-loop RO, about 0.9 V of headroom the 3.3 V rail does not have near the top of a 2.5 V step. Recorded because the datasheet SR number is quoted at 5 V into 50 pF and does not transfer. It costs nothing here - the board's own settling budget is 9.0 us against a 197 ns measured settle.

time for C_SAMPLE to come within 1/2 LSB (15.6 uV) of final after the 20 mV small-signal step, in ns. Measured 197 ns against the 9000 ns acquisition window - 46x of margin. Warning rather than error because the binding settling promise is made on the real switched-capacitor acquisition event in acquisition-settling.cir, not on a voltage step at the buffer input; this one bounds the buffer's own contribution to it.

raw peak at the BUFFER OUTPUT /AIN_BUF on the same 1 ns edge, feedforward spike included. Measured 11.7 %, which exceeds blocks.md s7 item 3's 5 % figure - and that number is reported rather than hidden. It is NOT loop ringing: it does not ring back (0.00013 %), and it scales with edge rate as a differentiator must (11.7 % at 1-10 ns, 8.2 % at 100 ns, 3.1 % at 300 ns, 0.94 % at 1 us), which identifies it as capacitive feedforward through Cdif = 5 pF - in a follower the inverting input IS the output node. The board cannot produce an edge anywhere near this fast: the tap drives the buffer input from a 240 kohm Thevenin into ~9 pF, so the fastest physical edge is ~2 us. The ceiling is set at 25 % so a genuine loop failure still trips here (the R6 -> 0 defect reads 73.4 %) without failing the gate on a known measurement artifact.
